challenges.title: After deployment
challenges.description: A demand forecast passed evaluation and has been deployed. What should the team do next?

choices.text: Monitor service health and data, and assess prediction quality when outcomes become available.
Stop monitoring because evaluation has already proved the model will always work.
Delete the records of the training data and model configuration.
Assume all future input data will match training data.

challenges.hint: Consider what can change after the model starts serving users.

solution.code: Monitor service health and data, and assess prediction quality when outcomes become available.

steps.title: Observe the service
steps.explanation: Availability and data problems can affect users even after a successful offline evaluation.

steps.title: Check outcomes
steps.explanation: When ground truth arrives, compare predictions with outcomes and investigate material changes.

challenges.title: Investigate an alert
challenges.description: A monitoring alert shows that many incoming feature values are missing after a pipeline change. What is the best first response?

choices.text: Remove all monitoring to prevent future alerts.
Investigate the input pipeline and assess the impact on predictions.
Ignore the alert because the model was accurate during evaluation.
Retrain immediately without checking why the values are missing.

challenges.hint: Identify whether the issue is in the data pipeline before choosing a remedy.

solution.code: Investigate the input pipeline and assess the impact on predictions.

steps.title: Find the cause
steps.explanation: A pipeline change can produce missing values even if the underlying population has not changed.

steps.title: Choose a response
steps.explanation: Understanding the cause and impact helps the team fix the pipeline or apply the appropriate safeguard.

challenges.title: Record an experiment
challenges.description: A dataset changes over time. Which record best helps a teammate reproduce a training run?

choices.text: Only the dataset's general name.
Only the final accuracy score.
The name of the person who ran the experiment, with no technical details.
The data version and split, code revision, settings, and environment.

challenges.hint: Record both the data used and how the run was executed.

solution.code: The data version and split, code revision, settings, and environment.

steps.title: Identify the inputs
steps.explanation: A version and split identify which data the experiment used.

steps.title: Capture execution details
steps.explanation: Code, settings, and environment provide the context needed to rerun or investigate the result.

challenges.title: Understand random seeds

choices.text: Different environments or nondeterministic operations can still affect the run.
A seed guarantees identical results across all hardware and libraries.
Recording a seed prevents the team from recording data versions.
The recorded seed automatically changes the target labels.

challenges.hint: A seed is useful, but it does not control every source of variation.

solution.code: Different environments or nondeterministic operations can still affect the run.

steps.title: Recognize the seed's role
steps.explanation: A seed controls some random choices, such as initialization when the implementation uses it.

steps.title: Account for other variation
steps.explanation: Hardware, dependency versions, and nondeterministic operations can still change results.

challenges.title: Trace a dataset change

choices.text: Only the name of the dashboard color theme.
Only the name of the model author.
The dataset version and preprocessing used by each run.
A statement that all datasets are permanently identical.

challenges.hint: Compare the inputs and transformations associated with the two runs.

solution.code: The dataset version and preprocessing used by each run.

steps.title: Compare the versions
steps.explanation: The recorded snapshots and transformations reveal whether the model saw different data.

steps.title: Investigate the change
steps.explanation: Lineage helps separate data changes from changes to code or configuration.

challenges.title: Version data responsibly

choices.text: Assume the request applies only to future model runs.
Apply the relevant deletion and retention rules to stored versions and document the impact.
Hide the snapshot from the catalog but retain the data without review.
Keep all copies forever because reproducibility always overrides privacy.

challenges.hint: Versioned snapshots remain subject to data governance requirements.

solution.code: Apply the relevant deletion and retention rules to stored versions and document the impact.

steps.title: Follow data obligations
steps.explanation: Access, retention, and deletion rules also apply to versioned snapshots.

steps.title: Identify the dependency

steps.title: Keep the mapping compatible

Delete the evaluation report.

steps.title: Inspect dependencies
steps.explanation: Different preprocessing can change the values passed to the model.

steps.title: Verify the package

challenges.title: Compare two training runs

choices.text: No settings, because defaults are always stable.

challenges.title: Reject invalid training settings

Start training and mark validation as passed.

steps.explanation: A batch size must be a valid positive count.
